Lesson 01

The ecosystem around a system you ship

Why it matters

A shipped assistant borrows a model, an index, a tool loop, a trace, a cloud account, and sometimes a voice stack. None of those own your policy.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
01 of 12
Time
12 min
Level
Core
Page
EX-01
Track
EX
Use
A shipped assistant borrows a model, an index, a tool loop, a trace, a cloud account, and sometimes a voice stack. None of those own your p…

The center is the system you are accountable for: the app, the policy, and the trace. Sister technologies plug into that center. They do not replace the owner of the data or the owner of the call.

Six families

  • Model providers compute the next token behind an API or a weight file.
  • Vector stores return neighbors. They do not decide that a chunk is true.
  • Orchestration is the loop: prompt, tool, observation, stop. MCP is a protocol inside that family.
  • Observability and evals tell you what happened and whether the change may ship.
  • Cloud accounts bill, isolate, and region-pin the run.
  • Voice stacks turn audio into text and back. The contact platform still owns the call.
FamilyJobDoes not own
ModelNext-token scoresYour corpus or your tools
VectorsNearest chunks under a filterThe decision to trust a chunk
LoopTool calls until a stop rulePermission to send, pay, or delete
EvalsThe same tasks, scored againA single pretty demo
CloudIdentity, region, billYour product policy
VoiceASR, turn-taking, TTSEmergency calling or the queue

Snapshot, not a lineup

Vendor model ids move. The 2026-10-14 study draft quoted specific ids from vendor pages. Those sentences stay in the rooms that cited them, and they were not re-fetched on 2026-10-15.

Check

What sits at the center of the map?

Show the answer

The system you are accountable for: app, policy, and trace. The six families are neighbors, not owners.

Lesson 02

Architecture from a prompt to a gate

Why it matters

Draw the path before you pick a vendor: input, policy, retrieval, model, tools, trace, and a person at every side effect.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
02 of 12
Time
14 min
Level
Core
Page
EX-02
Track
EX
Use
Draw the path before you pick a vendor: input, policy, retrieval, model, tools, trace, and a person at every side effect.

A fundamentals path is tokens, context, and sampling. An advanced path is the same path with a schema, a retrieved span, a tool allowlist, and a gate. The pictures differ. The habit does not.

Boxes you should be able to point at

  1. Caller or user, and the channel they are actually on.
  2. Policy: what data may leave the machine, and which actions need a person.
  3. Retriever: chunk id, score, and the refusal when the span is missing.
  4. Model: a pinned id, a token budget, and a timeout.
  5. Tools: name, schema, permission, and an idempotent handler.
  6. Trace: prompt version, retrieval ids, tool calls, latency, cost.
  7. Gate: quality, safety, latency, and cost on a versioned task set.

Demo architecture

A chat box with no retriever and no trace is a demo. Do not draw it as the production path.

Check

Where does a person sit in this architecture?

Show the answer

On every side effect: send, pay, delete, and any cutover. The model does not approve itself.

Lesson 03

Deployment and configuration walkthrough

Why it matters

Configure the run you can roll back: pinned ids, secrets outside the repo, a timeout, a log that omits raw private text, and a kill switch.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
03 of 12
Time
16 min
Level
Practice
Page
EX-03
Track
EX
Use
Configure the run you can roll back: pinned ids, secrets outside the repo, a timeout, a log that omits raw private text, and a kill switch.

Deployment here means the smallest hosted or local run that a second person can start from the README. It is not a cluster diagram.

Walkthrough

  1. Write the model id, the embedding id, and the prompt version in one config file.
  2. Put the API key in the environment or a secret store. Refuse to start if the key is inside the repo.
  3. Bind a local runner to loopback until you have a reason to expose it.
  4. Set a timeout and a retry cap. A retry must not double-send.
  5. Log request ids, token counts, retrieval ids, and tool names. Drop the key and the raw private text.
  6. Name the kill switch: the flag, the person who may throw it, and the old path you return to.
SettingSafe defaultCheck
Model idPinned snapshot, not a family nameThe id in the log matches the config
SecretsEnvironment or secret storeA repo search finds no key
TimeoutShorter than the user's patienceA hung call fails closed
LogIds and countsA sample line has no private paragraph

Unverified product screens

Console click-paths for a specific host were not re-checked on 2026-10-15. Use this list as the checklist, then confirm the screen in the vendor doc.

Check

What must a log line leave out?

Show the answer

The API key and the raw private text. Keep ids and counts.

Lesson 04

Migration and cutover from a legacy bot

Why it matters

Move off a rules bot or a pasted FAQ only when the new path wins on a written task set, with a rollback to the old bot.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
04 of 12
Time
16 min
Level
Practice
Page
EX-04
Track
EX
Use
Move off a rules bot or a pasted FAQ only when the new path wins on a written task set, with a rollback to the old bot.

Legacy here means the thing users already have: a decision tree, a keyword FAQ, a macro in the agent desktop, or a prompt with no eval. The cutover is a product change, not a model swap.

Checklist

  1. Inventory the answers the old bot gives and the source each answer is allowed to use.
  2. Write ten tasks the old bot fails, including a refusal and a boring case.
  3. Index only documents you are allowed to store. Record the embedding model id on the index.
  4. Run shadow mode: the new path answers beside the old one, and users still see the old one.
  5. Compare retrieval first. A better paragraph on the wrong chunk is not a win.
  6. Cut over a named audience. Keep the old bot one switch away.
  7. Stop the cutover if safety failures rise or if the trace goes blank.

Cutover plan

PhaseUsers seeExit
ShadowThe old botTen tasks scored, retrieval measured
LimitedThe new path, one queue or one teamNo new safety failures, kill switch tested
WiderThe new path, with the old bot still deployedA written rollback owner
RetireThe new pathThe old bot's tasks still live in the eval set

Check

When is the old bot allowed to leave?

Show the answer

After the limited audience holds and the old bot's tasks are still in the eval set. Not on demo day.

Lesson 05

Troubleshooting playbook

Why it matters

Split a bad answer into retrieval, the model, the tool, the policy, and the channel before you change a prompt.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
05 of 12
Time
14 min
Level
Practice
Page
EX-05
Track
EX
Use
Split a bad answer into retrieval, the model, the tool, the policy, and the channel before you change a prompt.

A playbook is a sequence you can follow at 2 a.m. Each step has a fact you can read in a log, not a hunch.

Order

  1. Read the trace. If there is no trace, stop and add one. You cannot debug a blank board.
  2. Check the retrieval pack. If the fact is absent, fix the index or refuse. Do not raise temperature.
  3. Check the tool result. If the handler erred, the model is quoting your bug.
  4. Check the policy. A refusal that should have fired is a gate bug, not a tone bug.
  5. Check latency by hop: network, retrieval, model, tool, and, on a phone, ASR and TTS.
  6. Change one thing. Rescore the same tasks. Write down the regression.
SymptomFirst place to lookDo not
Confident wrong factWas the span in the pack?Ask the model if it is sure
Blank answersTimeouts and the token budgetFine-tune
Double charge or double sendRetry and idempotencyAdd another agent
Slow phone turnASR, model, TTS, separatelyBlame 'the AI' as one hop

Check

What is the first move when the trace is empty?

Show the answer

Stop and add a trace. A prompt edit on a blank board does not explain the next failure.

Protocols here are the ones an AI system meets: HTTPS to a model API, a local runner, trace export, and, when the user is on a phone, SIP and RTP. MCP over stdio has no port. Remote MCP uses HTTP.

Study matrix

NamePortTransportStatus of this row
HTTPS model API443TCPThe usual web port. Confirm the vendor host.
DNS53UDP and TCPName lookup. Standard, still confirm your resolver.
OTLP gRPC4317TCPOpenTelemetry's documented default. Not re-fetched 2026-10-15.
OTLP HTTP4318TCPOpenTelemetry's documented default. Not re-fetched 2026-10-15.
Ollama default11434TCPThe project's widely published loopback default. Not re-fetched 2026-10-15. Bind it to localhost until you mean to share it.
SIP5060UDP and TCPRFC 3261. Confirm the listener you deploy.
SIP over TLS5061TCPThe commonly assigned TLS port. Confirm in the IANA registry before you lock a firewall.
RTP mediaa configured rangeUDPNot one universal port. The range is a design choice on your SBC.

Sources to open: RFC 3261 at rfc-editor.org, the OpenTelemetry OTLP spec at opentelemetry.io, the MCP specification at modelcontextprotocol.io, and the Ollama project docs. The IANA service registry is the place to confirm 5060 and 5061. Those pages were not re-fetched on 2026-10-15.

Pasting this matrix into a firewall is a mistake. It is a lesson. Your change ticket names the real hosts.

Ladder, for study

Check

Why is there no port on MCP stdio?

Show the answer

Stdio is a local process with a command, an environment, and a root folder. A port appears only when you choose HTTP.

Lesson 07

Voice bridge: SIP, PSTN, recording, WFM, and emergency calls

Why it matters

The phone system owns the call. A model may transcribe, suggest, or speak only inside the path that system already recorded and routed.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
07 of 12
Time
16 min
Level
Advanced
Page
EX-07
Track
EX
Use
The phone system owns the call. A model may transcribe, suggest, or speak only inside the path that system already recorded and routed.

Bring-your-own-carrier and SIP trunking are decisions on the voice platform: who provides numbers, who handles signaling, and who carries media. This AI course does not design your dial plan. The UC, Webex, Connect, and SIP labs are the places for that craft.

What the model is allowed to touch

  • A transcript, after the voice platform has the audio.
  • A suggested reply a person can send, or a spoken reply the platform plays.
  • A retrieval over notes you are allowed to store.
  • A transfer back to a person, requested through the platform's tool, not by the model inventing a route.

Sister systems

SystemJobAI course limit
SIP trunk / PSTN / BYOCNumbers and the carrier pathName the owner. Do not invent trunk groups here.
Recording and quality managementWhat was said, and how it is scoredConsent and retention are policy. Thresholds are product facts to read on that vendor's page.
Workforce managementForecast and scheduleA model does not replace the forecast. Specific vendor windows in the contact-center rooms were not re-fetched on 2026-10-15.
E911 / emergencyA telephony dutyAn assistant must not be the only path to emergency services. This course does not certify a deployment.

Emergency calls

If a caller needs emergency help, the voice platform's emergency path is the path. Do not send that turn to a model and hope.

Check

Who owns an emergency call?

Show the answer

The voice platform's emergency path. The model is not that path.

Lesson 08

CRM, analytics, and API bridges

Why it matters

Integrate by writing a ticket id, a retrieval id, and a tool result into the system of record. Do not paste a customer logo and call it a partnership.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
08 of 12
Time
14 min
Level
Practice
Page
EX-08
Track
EX
Use
Integrate by writing a ticket id, a retrieval id, and a tool result into the system of record. Do not paste a customer logo and call it a p…

This campus claims no customer deployment. A real integration is a pattern you can test: the CRM already has the case, the assistant reads fields it is allowed to read, and it writes back only through a tool a person approved.

Pattern

  1. The system of record creates the id. The model does not invent the case number.
  2. The tool schema lists the fields. Extra fields are a bug.
  3. Analytics count tasks, refusals, handoffs, latency, and cost. A vanity 'containment' number without a definition is not a metric.
  4. Webhooks retry. The handler is idempotent.
  5. Cross-platform bridges (a contact desktop, a CRM, a chat channel) share the trace id. They do not share a single vendor's admin model.

No customer story

No logo, no seat count, and no 'we did this for a bank' claim belongs in this course. If you have a deployment, the proof is your own trace, under your employer's rules.

Check

Who creates the case id?

Show the answer

The system of record. The model reads it. It does not mint it.

Lesson 09

AI agents beside a human queue

Why it matters

An agent is a loop with a schema, a step cap, and a trace. In a contact center it sits beside the queue. It does not become the queue.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
09 of 12
Time
12 min
Level
Advanced
Page
EX-09
Track
EX
Use
An agent is a loop with a schema, a step cap, and a trace. In a contact center it sits beside the queue. It does not become the queue.

The agents track teaches the loop. This page is the boundary: the queue still has an arrival, a wait, and a person. The bot may greet, retrieve, and draft. Transfer is a tool the platform runs.

  • Write the done-check before the loop starts.
  • Cap the steps. A loop that will not stop is a bill.
  • Ask before send, pay, delete, or a change to the customer's record.
  • Put the handoff in the trace: why the person got the turn, and what the person received.

Check

What does the queue still own?

Show the answer

Arrival, wait, and the person. The agent loop does not replace that ownership.

Lesson 10

Security, compliance, and the limits of this course

Why it matters

Write the data you will store, the tools you will allow, and the actions that always need a person. This course is not a certification and not legal advice.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
10 of 12
Time
14 min
Level
Advanced
Page
EX-10
Track
EX
Use
Write the data you will store, the tools you will allow, and the actions that always need a person. This course is not a certification and …

Useful public anchors, which you should read yourself: the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (airc.nist.gov), the OWASP GenAI security project (genai.owasp.org), and the privacy law that actually applies to your users. Naming them is not compliance.

  • Treat retrieved text as untrusted. It can carry instructions.
  • A debug log is a database. Retention is a decision.
  • Card data, health data, and children's data need the regime that governs them. Do not guess the scope from a blog.
  • A jailbreak story in a lesson is not permission to build the attack.

Not a certification

Nothing in this campus makes you certified, and nothing here is a finding about your employer.

Check

Is this course legal advice or a certificate?

Show the answer

No. It is a study text. The regime that applies to your users is a document you read, not a paragraph you memorize here.

Lesson 11

Licensing, certification, and a career path

Why it matters

This course issues no certificate. Vendor exams change. The portfolio that matters is a trace, a task set, and a written gate.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
11 of 12
Time
12 min
Level
Core
Page
EX-11
Track
EX
Use
This course issues no certificate. Vendor exams change. The portfolio that matters is a trace, a task set, and a written gate.

Model weights and vendor docs keep their own licenses. The code in this repository is under the MIT file at the repo root. The footer states a content license the mission brief asked for. Those two statements are both visible; do not assume they have been reconciled by a lawyer.

A path you can show

  1. Fundamentals: explain a token, a window, and a sample without a product name.
  2. Build: a grounded assistant on notes you may use, with one read-only tool.
  3. Prove: ten tasks, a retrieval score, a safety count, latency, and cost.
  4. Interview: the drills in the interview track. Say the mechanism, the control, and the evidence.
  5. Optional: a vendor exam, read from that vendor's current page. This course will not guess the passing score.

Check

What should you show instead of a certificate from this site?

Show the answer

A trace, a versioned task set, and a gate you can defend.

Lesson 12

Roadmap and what was not re-checked

Why it matters

Study the mechanisms. Treat dated product claims as a snapshot unless you open the page.

Try it: Quiz and boss exam

Lesson
12 of 12
Time
10 min
Level
Core
Page
EX-12
Track
EX
Use
Study the mechanisms. Treat dated product claims as a snapshot unless you open the page.

What is stable enough to learn: next-token prediction, retrieval then generation, tool schemas, eval gates, and the habit of pinning ids. Papers this campus already cites: Vaswani et al. 2017, Lewis et al. 2020, Hu et al. 2021.

What was not re-fetched on 2026-10-15: vendor model lists quoted in the 2026-10-14 rooms, contact-center product steps, prices, context-window numbers, and certification catalogs. Each of those rooms carries a note. If a sentence has no note and no link, do not treat it as a fresh fact.

  • Future hook: a new model id is a config change plus a rescore, not a new course.
  • Future hook: a new channel (voice, chat, desktop) reuses the trace id and the same gate.
  • Future hook: a sister lab (UC, Webex, Connect, SIP) owns the telephony. Link to it. Do not copy it into this course.

Check

What do you do when a model id in a lesson looks stale?

Show the answer

Open the cited page, pin the id you actually call, and rescore the same tasks.
